text: According to Shaivite tradition, once upon a time, Lord Shiva wished to stay away from the world in peace.
He took the form of a deer in the forests of Nepal.
The Devas, searching for Him, eventually recognized that deer as Lord Shiva Himself.
In their attempt to stop Him, one of the deer's horns broke off.
The Sthalapuranam (local legend) states that Lord Shiva manifested as Pashupatinath in that very sacred spot.
The name "Pashupati" holds an even deeper meaning.
In Sanatana Dharma, "Pashu" does not merely mean an animal.
It refers to every living being entangled in the bonds of ignorance, ego, and delusion.
The Lord who shows the path to liberation for every such being is Pashupatinath.
